newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B share index ends up on rise hopes.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B share index ends up on rise hopes.

text.p: Shanghai's B share index closed up sharply in active trading on Friday helped by institutional buying on hopes of further rises after the two-week holiday starting next Monday, traders said.
The index jumped 1.065 points or 1.62 percent to 66.849 points, on volume of 22.9 million shares worth $10.2 million, up from Thursday's $6.7 million.
The Shanghai Stock Exchange will be closed for the Chinese lunar new year market holiday from Monday, February 3 until Monday, February 17.
Brokers said domestic investors bought shares actively in the belief that overseas investors will come back into the market after the long holiday.
"Window-dressing buying supported the market with investors believing the market will go forward with overseas fund flowing in after the new year break," one broker said.
"The index is likely to rise to the 68-point level after the holiday," a second broker said.
All 43 B shares traded, with 34 up, four flat and five down.
Industrial Sewing Machine was the star on speculative buying, rising $0.008 or 4.76 percent to $0.176 on volume of 51,000 shares.
Market barometer property developer Lujiazui followed on window-dressing buying by institutions, rising $0.036 or 4.37 percent to $0.858 on volume of 2.0 million shares.
Huaxin Cement was the most active share on institutional buying on talk of improved 1996 results, gaining $0.006 or 2.12 percent to $0.288 volume of 2.5 million shares.
Shanghai's A share market moved up modestly with most investors staying on the sidelines in the last session before the Chinese new year, brokers said.

The A index inched up 4.425 points or 0.44 percent to 1006.362 points, on volume of 357.5 million shares worth 3.5 billion yuan. The SSE 30 index gained 20.908 points or 0.80 percent to 2620.313 points.
Chengdu People's Store was the star on buying in the late session, closing up 0.70 yuan or 5.69 percent to 13.00 yuan on volume of 1.4 million shares.
